transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-16
Time: 10:00 PT
Duration: 45 min
Title: POC Weekly Sync - model selection & pinning
Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Aisha (CS), Maya (Orion Head of ML), Luis (Platform), Hannah (PM)

Summary: quick recap then deep dive on model pinning, canary and fallback paths, and action items.

[00:00] Jamie: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45, agenda is quick - results review and finalizing which model to pin for the pilot, and how we do rollbacks/fallbacks.
[00:18] Maya: yes, thanks. we've run the test harness you sent, got the 500-sample runs, and some of the outputs on v1.4 look better semantically but latency is creeping up.
[00:30] Samir: right, the v1.4 non-quantized does give higher perplexity improvements but p95 latency is ~420ms on your instance vs v1.3 at ~270ms. we suspect kernel selection on that specific sequence length distribution is causing the delta.
[00:50] Luis: hmm that p95 is a concern for customer-facing flows. our SLA target for the feature is 300ms p95.
[01:04] Jamie: correct, so two knobs: we can pin to v1.3 for now for predictable latency, or pin to v1.4 but use a canary and automatic fallback to v1.3 if p95 goes above 350.
[01:22] Hannah: can you explain fallback behavior? like will requests reroute mid-session, is there KV cache implications?
[01:34] Samir: good question. fallback is per-request routing. there's implications for KV cache—if you switch model families mid-conversation you lose KV cache compatibility, so you'll want to use fallback for idempotent single-turn calls or accept ephemeral context loss. we can also configure prefix caching and sticky routing for multi-turn sessions.
[01:56] Maya: so for chat we probably need sticky routing, can't afford context loss. for our summary endpoint single-turns, fallback is fine.
[02:08] Jamie: makes sense. our recommended pattern: pin chat routes to v1.3-stable with occasional v1.4 canary for quality eval; pin single-turn summarization to v1.4 with fallback to a quantized v1.3-q if latency spikes.
[02:26] Luis: what's v1.3-q? is that a quantized variant you host? any accuracy hit?
[02:36] Samir: v1.3-q is a 4-bit quantized variant we tested. small accuracy regressions on some edge cases but within your acceptance thresholds in the eval set. big win on latency/cost—p50 down by ~30% and token cost down ~25%.
[02:54] Maya: acceptable for low-risk outputs. for any compliance-sensitive output we should route to non-quantized. does Redwood support per-route policies?
[03:06] Jamie: yes, per-route pinning and policy overrides are supported in the console and API. you can set canary %, fallback targets, and per-route caching.
[03:18] Hannah: on rollout cadence, how fast can we toggle pinning? if we detect regression do we manually rollback or is there an auto fallback?
[03:30] Samir: you can do both. we have automatic SLO-based fallback rules: e.g., if p95 latency > X or error rate > Y over N minutes, route new requests to fallback target. manual rollback is also one-click in the console.
[03:50] Luis: detail on metrics: how do we get the p95 from your side vs our infra?
[03:58] Aisha: we emit per-request traces + aggregated histograms into the console. we can also forward traces to your Datadog/Prometheus. we'll send our benchmark spreadsheet so you can compare raw logs.
[04:12] Maya: perfect. about catalog comparisons — we compared Redwood's v1.3/v1.4 to Anthropic on our prompts, Anthropic was strong on instruction following but cost was higher; OpenAI had good latency but less control around private deployment.
[04:30] Jamie: that's consistent with what others see. Redwood's catalog also includes quantized family variants and we recommend pinning model ids (exact version strings) rather than friendly names to avoid surprise changes.
[04:42] Samir: yes, pinning example: model_id = redwood-1.3.2 and canary = redwood-1.4-beta. pin the route to the explicit model_id. console shows exact SHA and kernel profile.
[04:56] Hannah: is the model_id immutable? what if you need a security patch?
[05:02] Samir: by design model_ids are immutable; patches produce a new model_id. we also support aliasing in applying an alias to multiple ids for staged rollouts but we recommend explicit pinning in pilots.
[05:20] Maya: and rollback—do you have cold-start impact when switching targets?
[05:26] Samir: some warmup happens for kernels and KV caches. if you're switching within same model family it's faster; between families you may see cold-token overhead for the first few requests. that's another reason to use sticky routing for multi-turn.
[05:44] Luis: ok. security check — we need SOC2 and KMS notes for the private pilot. are those publicly available?
[05:52] Jamie: yes, I'll send the security pack after the call; includes SOC 2 Type II scope, network diagram, KMS integrations, and redaction/retention policies.
[06:04] Maya: great. one more—data residency; Orion wants EU data to stay in eu-west. can we route by region?
[06:12] Samir: yes, request routing by region is supported and you can pin model variants in region. for Private (VPC) deployments we can run in your cloud region too.
[06:22] Hannah: cost—can we see per-token breakdown per model? that will help PM decide which to prioritize.
[06:30] Aisha: we have token-level cost breakdowns in the console and a CSV export. Samir will run a 1k-sample and produce a cost/latency sheet for v1.3, v1.3-q, v1.4.
[06:42] Maya: what's your recommendation given our SLA of 300ms p95 and tight budget?
[06:48] Samir: recommend pinning chat to v1.3-stable for pilot to meet SLA. For single-turn summarization pin to v1.4-beta with fallback to v1.3-q. Then run a canary for v1.4 on 5% traffic for 48 hours and measure quality/regressions. If quality delta is > your acceptance threshold we keep fallback.
[07:10] Hannah: and how do we capture quality? by prompt set scoring?
[07:14] Maya: yes, we'll provide 10 gold prompts and expected outputs; canary results will be scored automatically.
[07:22] Luis: timeline—when do we start the canary?
[07:25] Jamie: once Samir shares the 1k benchmark and you confirm acceptance criteria — aim for next Wednesday 2026-03-24.
[07:34] Maya: sounds good. small nit — the transcripts sometimes have name errors in your export. just flagging because we use the verbatim outputs for evaluation.
[07:42] Aisha: noted, we try to keep exports consistent; will include raw audio IDs if you need to re-transcribe.
[07:50] Hannah: any blockers on VPC peering? Luis?
[07:53] Luis: need a few network details for our infra team, I'll share peering CIDR and an engineer to coordinate. target by 2026-03-22.
[08:02] Jamie: great. recap then next steps.
[08:06] Jamie: recap — pin chat routes to redwood-1.3.<number> stable; pin summarization to redwood-1.4-beta with fallback to redwood-1.3-q; canary 5% for 48 hours starting ~2026-03-24 pending benchmark results; Samir runs 1k-sample and shares spreadsheet; Jamie shares security docs and pricing; customer to provide 10 gold prompts and VPC details.
[08:26] Maya: agreed. thanks team.
[08:29] Samir: I'll kick off the 1k job after this and share the sheet by Friday.
[08:33] Jamie: thanks all, we'll follow up in email.

References/shared artifacts: 1) benchmark spreadsheet link: https://redwood.example.com/share/orion-poc-benchmarks-03-16 (demo link), 2) security pack link: https://redwood.example.com/sec/orion-soc2-2026 (private), 3) rollout playbook (short note)
